$comment: Allow-list for the axe passes in e2e/a11y.spec.ts.
Every entry is a DEFERRAL, not an absolution: it names one axe rule, the
pass and routes it applies to, and a node-level predicate that must match.
A violation is only suppressed when EVERY one of its nodes is matched by
some exception — a single unmatched node fails the test and prints the
node. That is what makes this a ratchet: the known failures stay quiet,
but any NEW node (a different colour pair, a different element) is red.
An exception without a predicate (no `contrast`, no `htmlIncludes`) is
rejected at load time, so nobody can accidentally mute a whole rule.
Fields:
id            — stable handle, used in the 'unused exception' report
pass          — 'preview' (the [data-docs-preview] region) or
'code' (the CodeExample CodePanel: toolbar + Shiki)
rule          — axe rule id
routes        — primitive slugs this applies to, or '*' for all
contrast      — for color-contrast: the exact fg/bg pair axe computed
htmlIncludes  — every string must appear in the node's outerHTML
reason        — why this is not fixed here
ref           — where the decision / follow-up lives
When a row gets fixed, delete its entry — the suite reports exceptions
that no longer match anything at the end of a full run.

exceptions.reason: Shiki `punctuation` / `meta.brace` / `punctuation.separator|terminator` / `meta.tag.start|end` render at #9a968e on the #fbfaf6 panel ground = 2.82:1 (AA needs 4.5:1). Deliberately deferred: comments already sit at the ramp's light limit, so darkening the very frequent punctuation is a coordinated ramp/aesthetic decision (light needs L<=0.173, dark L>=0.247), not a drive-by recolour. The fg colour is unique to those scopes in shiki-editorial-themes.ts, so this pair matches the punctuation tokens and nothing else.
exceptions.ref: docs/technical-debt.md -> 'docs `CodePanel` Shiki punctuation token is below WCAG AA in both themes'

exceptions.reason: PRE-EXISTING, surfaced (not caused) by widening this harness. #00845c is NOT the library's --color-primary (that is oklch(0.52 0.15 240), blue) — it is --room-accent from the docs app's Rooms skin (apps/docs/src/lib/style/rooms-docs.css:77), which remaps --color-primary. So this is the docs site rendering every filled primary control at 4.25:1, not a library token defect: blocks' own contrast.test.ts covers the library pairs and passes. Fixing means re-picking the room accent (or its on-colour) — an apps/docs skin decision.
